title: Build apartments and commercial buildings to the building code (NCC Volume One)
what: Carry out building work on Class 2 to 9 buildings in accordance with the Building Code of Australia (NCC Volume One, with the NSW variations), a condition of every development consent and complying development certificate for building work. The edition in force is NCC 2022 until NCC 2025 is adopted on 1 May 2027. Its schedule in NCC 2025 varies 188 national provisions, the most of any state, 91 of them in special use buildings (Section I) and 30 in energy efficiency.

confidence_note: The law's own words require building or plumbing work to comply with the code. Drafted on 27 November 2026 for the NCC work (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N3); the variation counts are from the NCC 2025 dataset. Quoted from the corpus copy of the official text (NSW register as at early 2025).

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume One) as New South Wales applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
